name: Hadamard matrix conjecture
question: Does a real Hadamard matrix exist for every positive order divisible by four?
dispatch_next: Import a published construction for the smallest remaining engine gap, 188. This is an implementation gap, not an open existence case; the smallest order without a known matrix is 2396 after the 2026 verified constructions (arXiv:2610.27175).
dispatch_why: The engine now constructs orders 116, 156 and 172; its next gap is 188, a known constructed order. Published exact verifications cover every multiple of four below 2000; 2396 is the smallest currently without a known matrix (arXiv:2610.27175).

campaign.method: Algebraic constructions (Sylvester, Paley, Williamson, propus) with exact orthogonality certificates
campaign.hypothesis: A Hadamard matrix exists for every order divisible by 4.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: Name the smallest order 4k > 172 that this engine still does not build, and import one published quadruple for it.
campaign.next_experiment: Import a published construction for the smallest remaining engine gap, 188. This is an implementation gap, not an open existence case; the smallest order without a known matrix is 2396 after the 2026 verified constructions (arXiv:2610.27175).
campaign.falsification: A proof that no Hadamard matrix of some order 4k exists; a finite search failure is not sufficient.
campaign.blocker: Every order 4k <= 172 is now explicit in this engine; its next gap is 188. The common-multiplier Williamson search at n = 29 is a proved dead end, but 668 was settled by a verified 2026 construction. The smallest currently unknown order is 2396.

probes.name: Hadamard matrix conjecture
probes.title: Exact Hadamard matrices from Sylvester, Paley I/II and Kronecker products
probes.frontier: Known: Hadamard matrices exist for every order 4k < 2000. Order 668, formerly the smallest open case after order 428, was constructed in August 2026 and independently verified by Egan et al. (arXiv:2610.27175, 19 October 2026). The smallest order without a known matrix is now 2396. Orders 116, 156 and 172 are published propus quadruples (arXiv:1503.04226, arXiv:1708.05098). Engine gaps below are NOT open cases.

smoke.scope: Explicit (+1/-1) matrices with H H^T = nI for 32 of the 32 orders 4k <= 128 (the rest are engine gaps, not open cases).

deep.scope: Explicit (+1/-1) matrices with H H^T = nI for 91 of the 100 orders 4k <= 400 (the rest are engine gaps, not open cases).

milestones.title: Exact Hadamard matrices for every order 4k <= 172, including 116, 156 and 172
milestones.scope: Known constructions; not a new matrix and not a proof that every multiple of 4 works
milestones.description: Sylvester, Paley I/II, Williamson n=23 (order 92), and published propus quadruples for orders 116, 156 and 172, closed under Kronecker products. Each matrix is checked as H H^T = nI. Smoke covers all 32 orders 4k <= 128. Deep covers 91 of the 100 orders 4k <= 400; the first remaining engine gap is 188. Order 668 was constructed and independently verified in 2026; 2396 is now the smallest order without a known matrix (arXiv:2610.27175).

formal_statement.encodes: For every k ≥ 1 an Int matrix of order 4k with ±1 entries and pairwise orthogonal rows.

kernel_checked.claim: Explicit Hadamard matrices of orders 4, 8 (Sylvester) and 12 (Paley), re-checked by the kernel (order_4, order_8, order_12).
